transcribed_question:
1) the painted blue part corresponds to what vertebrae? Ans: T4/ T5 vertebrae
2) list event that occur at this angle Ans: Articulation of 2nd costal cartilage to the sternum, Separation of Sup. & Inf. mediastinum, Ending of Ascending aorta, Beginning of descending aorta, arch of aorta, bifurcation of trachea, terminate of Azygos V. to S.V.C

marker.description: Blue paint on the manubrium of the sternum

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the blue paint.
main_explanation: The blue paint highlights the superior portion of the sternum, which is the manubrium. It forms the upper part of the breastbone and articulates with the clavicles and the first pair of ribs.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following structures is located at the sternal angle (angle of Louis)?
options: Bifurcation of the common carotid artery
Origin of the inferior vena cava
supporting_question.explanation: The sternal angle is a key landmark where the manubrium meets the body of the sternum. It corresponds to the level of the T4/T5 intervertebral disc and marks the bifurcation of the trachea, the arch of the aorta, and the separation of the superior and inferior mediastinum.

true_false.statement: The sternal angle marks the articulation of the second costal cartilage with the sternum.
true_false.explanation: The sternal angle is the junction between the manubrium and the body of the sternum. It is the point where the second pair of ribs (via their costal cartilages) attaches to the sternum, making it a useful landmark for counting ribs.
